summary: Richard Hauschild (1901–1972) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied under Johannes Hertel and Albert Debrunner at Leipzig, Tübingen, and Jena. He served as Lektor at the University of Jena in 1938 and became an ordentliches Mitglied of the Saxon Academy of Sciences and Humanities (1949–1972).

Richard Henebry (1863–1916) was a linguist. He studied at St. John's College, St Patrick's Pontifical University, Maynooth (~1887–1892), University of Greifswald under Heinrich Zimmer (~1896–1898), and University of Freiburg (~1898).

Richard Hugh Robinson (1926–1970) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Alberta, SOAS, and the University of London under David Snellgrove, Arthur Waley, and David Friedman. He founded and taught at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (professor, 1961).

Richard Hughes Seager (born 1948) is a religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Wisconsin System, Harvard Divinity School, and Harvard University (PhD ~1982–1987). He served as Associate Professor of Religion at Hamilton College (~1994–2014).

Richard J. Davidson (born 1951) studied at Midwood High School, New York University (~1968–1972), and Harvard University (~1972–1976). He held posts at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1987 and 1996, serving there as psychology professor from 2001 to 2017.

Richard Jay Kohn (1948–2000) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1988, having studied under doctoral supervisor Geshe Lhundub Sopa and traditional teacher Lama Tharchin Rinpoche.

Richard K. Payne (born 1949) works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies, having studied under Chisei Aratano and Taisen Miyata. He was Dean at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (~1993–2017) and held posts at the Graduate Theological Union and University of Chicago.

Richard Keith Sprigg (1922–2011) was a linguist and Tibetologist who attended Oakham School (~1935–1940). He held long-term academic posts at the University of London and SOAS University of London (~1948–1980).

Richard Kieckhefer (born 1946) is a religious studies and history scholar. He studied at Saint Louis University, University of Texas at Austin, and Monumenta Germaniae Historica. Since 1975, he has held professorships in history and religious studies at Northwestern University.

Richard King (born 1965) is a scholar of religious studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at Dalhousie, McGill, and Lancaster University under Daniel Mariau. He held academic posts at the University of Stirling, Vanderbilt University, and the University of Glasgow.
Richard M. Eaton (born 1940) is a scholar of history and Indology. He studied at the College of Wooster (~1958–1962) and served as Professor of History at the University of Arizona from around 1972.

Richard M. Jaffe (born 1954) is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He held an academic post at North Carolina State University (~1995–2001) and later at Duke University (attested ~2001).

Richard Mahoney is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Canterbury under Paul Harrison, completing his Master of Arts by 2002, and also held an affiliation there in 2001.

Richard Morris (1833–1894) was an Indology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies scholar educated at Battersea. He served as master at Dedham Grammar School, lecturer at King's College School, headmaster at the Royal Masonic School for Boys, and ex-president of the Philological Society.

Richard P. Boyle completed graduate studies at the University of Washington and studied under Kyozan Joshu Sasaki. He taught at the University of California, Los Angeles, and held a post at the University of New Mexico (attested 2015).

Richard P. Hayes (born 1945) works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He earned a doctorate at the University of Toronto under Bimal Krishna Matilal, and held posts at the University of Toronto, McGill University, and the University of New Mexico.
Richard Peter Hottelet is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Narayan Hemandas Samtani and held a post at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (both attested in 1971).

Richard Phené Spiers (1838–1916) was a scholar in history and archaeology. He studied at King's College London from around 1856 to 1858 and at the École Nationale Supérieure des Beaux-Arts from around 1858 to 1861.

Richard Pischel (1849–1908) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and Albrecht Weber at Breslau. He held professorships at Kiel, Halle, and Berlin, and served as librarian for the Deutsche Morgenländische Gesellschaft.

Richard Polenberg (1937–2020) was an American history scholar. He studied at Brooklyn College and Columbia University. He served as Professor of American History at Cornell University (1966–2011) and was a Fulbright Visiting Professor at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1986–1987).
